'''Jeremiah Oljawain Martin Jr.''' (born June 19, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]].

==Early life==
Martin grew up in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] and [[Mitchell High School (Tennessee)|Mitchell High School]]. He was a three year starter for the school's basketball team and Mitchell won the [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association|TSSAA]] Class A state season in his junior and senior seasons. As a senior, Martin was named [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] and the MVP of the TSSAA State Tournament after scoring 19 points in the state title game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dnj.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/03/14/mitchell-wins-state-title/24787407/|title=Memphis Mitchell repeats as Class A boys champion|work=[[The Daily News Journal]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 14, 2015|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> Martin initially committed to playing college basketball for [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]], but de-committed in favor of playing for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/on-the-sidelines/2015/04/11/former-tech-commit-jeremiah-martin-flips-to-memphis/25652953/|title=Former Tech commit Jeremiah Martin flips to Memphis|first=Sean|last=Isabella|work=[[The News-Star]]|date=April 11, 2015|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Martin played four seasons for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. He appeared in 29 games as a freshman, starting five, and averaged 2.7 points and 1.2 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.memphisflyer.com/TigerBlue/archives/2019/03/04/jeremiahs-time|title=Jeremiah's Time|first=Frank|last=Murtaugh|work=[[Memphis Flyer]]|date=March 4, 2019|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> He became the team's starting point guard as a sophomore, averaging 10.3 points per game and leading the Tigers with 4.4 assists and 1.8 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.memphisdailynews.com/news/2017/jul/21/jeremiah-martin-no-rest-for-the-memphis-tigers-weary-point-guard/|title=Jeremiah Martin: No Rest for The Memphis Tigers' Weary Point Guard|first=Don|last=Wade|work=[[The Daily News (Memphis)|The Daily News]]|date=July 21, 2017|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> As a junior, Martin averaged 18.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists and an [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC)-leading 2.3 steals per game and was named second team All-AAC, despite missing seven games due to a foot injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2018/08/29/memphis-jeremiah-martin-emergency-hernia-surgery/1133284002/|title=Memphis guard Jeremiah Martin undergoes surgery to repair hernia|first=Drew|last=Will|work=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|date=August 29, 2018|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> In his senior season, Martin started all 36 of Memphis's games and was named first team All-AAC after averaging 19.7 points, 4.4 assists, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.19 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://929espn.radio.com/articles/jeremiah-martin-signs-nba-deal-miami-heat|title=Former Tiger Jeremiah Martin Signs NBA Deal with the Miami Heat|website=[[WMFS-FM|929ESPN.Radio.com]]|date=July 11, 2019|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> Martin led the team in points with 708 (the second most by a senior in Memphis history), as well as field goals (220), free throws made (202), assists (157), steals (79) and minutes played (1,236). He became the first player in school history with multiple 40-point games after scoring 41 points (all in the second half) against [[2018–19 South Florida Bulls men's basketball team|South Florida]] on February 2, 2019 and a career-high 43 against [[2018–19 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]] on February 20, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tri-statedefender.com/jeremiah-martin-impresses-the-miami-heat/07/17/|title=Jeremiah Martin impresses the Miami Heat|first=Terry|last=Davis|work=[[Tri-State Defender]]|date=July 17, 2019|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> He finished his collegiate career 10th in school history with 1,625 points scored and 436 assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wreg.com/2019/04/21/martin-earns-all-tournament-team-honors-at-portsmouth-invitational-tournament/|title=Martin earns All-Tournament team honors at Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|first=Megan|last=Rice|website=[[WREG-TV|WREG.com]]|date=April 21, 2019|access-date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> After his senior season Martin participated in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]] and was named to the All-Tournament team after averaging 15 points, 5.6 assists and 5.3 rebounds per game in three games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/4620/Jeremiah-Martin-named-to-All-Tournament-team-at-Portsmouth-Invitational|title=Jeremiah Martin named to All-Tournament team at Portsmouth Invitational|first=Jonah|last=Jordan|work=The Daily Memphian|date=April 22, 2019|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2019–2020)===
Martin worked out for several teams leading up to the [[2019 NBA draft]], but ultimately went unselected. He was named to the [[Miami Heat]]'s [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] roster and averaged 7.7 points and 2.3 assists in seven games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Oyefusi|title=Former Memphis basketball player Jeremiah Martin reflects on NBA summer league play|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2019/07/16/memphis-basketball-jeremiah-martin-miami-heat-nba-summer-league/1749095001/|date=July 16, 2019|work=The Commercial Appeal|access-date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> Martin signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Miami Heat]] on July 12, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ira|last=Winderman|title=Heat sign Chris Silva, Jeremiah Martin to camp contracts|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-signings-20190712-uampmxt74zfrtmmnnlokgvlizy-story.html|date=July 12, 2019|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|access-date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> On October 15, 2019, Martin was waived by the Heat.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT Waives Martin And Mulder|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waives-martin-and-mulder|date=October 15, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 16, 2019}}</ref> Following training camp, Martin was added to the roster of the Heat's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Skyforce Announces 2019–20 Training Camp Roster|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/|date=October 27, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 2, 2019|archive-date=November 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102180042/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 30, he tallied 31 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal in a win over the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremiah Martin: Erupts for 31 Saturday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jeremiah-martin-erupts-for-31-saturday/|date=December 1, 2019|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=February 1, 2020}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2020)===
On January 15, 2020, Martin was signed by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Jeremiah Martin to Two-way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/15/brooklyn-nets-sign-jeremiah-martin-to-two-way-contract|date=January 16, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> On January 22, Martin contributed 24 points, five rebounds, four assists, four steals and a block in a win over the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nets' Jeremiah Martin: Efficient in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-jeremiah-martin-efficient-in-win/|date=January 23, 2020|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=January 25, 2020}}</ref> Martin made his NBA debut on January 31 against the [[Chicago Bulls]], playing two minutes and grabbing a rebound in a 133–118 win. Martin scored his first career points on February 5, scoring two points on one for three shooting with one assist and one steal in the final nine minutes of a 129–88 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/martije02/gamelog/2020|title=Jeremiah Martin 2019-20 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> On August 11, he scored a career high 24 points in a 108–96 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://netswire.usatoday.com/2020/08/11/jeremiah-martin-among-nets-to-set-a-career-high-vs-magic/|title=Jeremiah Martin among Nets to set a career-high vs. Magic|date=August 11, 2020|website=netswire.usatoday.com|access-date=August 12, 2020}}</ref> Martin was waived just prior to the start of the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-sign Chris Chiozza to Two-way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/12/22/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-chris-chiozza-two-way-contract|date=December 22, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 22, 2020|quote=In a related move, Brooklyn has requested waivers on guard Jeremiah Martin.}}</ref>

===Long Island Nets (2021)===
On January 27, 2021, Martin re-signed with the Long Island Nets<ref>{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-2021-roster/|date=January 27, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 28, 2021}}</ref> where he appeared in 15 games, all starts and averaged 18.5 points, 3.7 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.4 steals in 31.8 minutes.<ref name="CLE2W">{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Jeremiah Matrin to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/martin-two-way-210428|date=April 28, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 28, 2021}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2021)===
On April 28, 2021, Martin signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="CLE2W" />

And the next off-season, Martin joined the [[New York Knicks]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=New York Notes: Tucker, Thor, Duarte, Knicks Front Office, Martin|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/07/new-york-notes-tucker-thor-duarte-knicks-front-office-martin.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 23, 2021|access-date=July 23, 2021}}</ref> and the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2021 NBA summer league]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|access-date=August 8, 2021|website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===New Zealand Breakers (2021–2022)===
On October 3, 2021, Martin signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-sign-former-nets-and-cavs-guard-jeremiah-martin|title=Breakers Sign former Nets and Cavs guard Jeremiah Martin|work=NBL.com.au|date=October 3, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}}</ref> On February 10, 2022, he parted ways with the Breakers. Martin averaged 12.3 points, 2.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists over ten games with the Breakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-martin-agree-release-with-randle-upgraded|title=Breakers, Martin Agree Release with Randle Upgraded|work=NBL.com.au|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}}</ref>

===Śląsk Wrocław (2022–2023)===
On August 13, 2022, he has signed with [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]] of the [[Polish Basketball League|PLK]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/slask-wroclaw-announce-signings-of-jeremiah-martin-and-artsiom-parakhouski/|title=Slask Wroclaw announce signings of Jeremiah Martin and Artsiom Parakhouski|work=Sportando |date=August 13, 2022|language=En|access-date=August 17, 2022}}</ref>

===Enisey Krasnoyarsk===
He has signed with [[BC Enisey|Enisey Krasnoarsk]] in the [[VTB United League]].
